claims.statement: Running the application locally is Docker Compose only (`cp .env.example .env` then `docker compose up -d`), and every backend or frontend development command must execute inside its container via `docker compose exec <backend|frontend> <command>`; the Go microservices are the exception — their checks run on the host Go toolchain (`gofmt`, `staticcheck`, `go vet`, `go test ./...`) or through the `just` recipes, and CI runs the same checks for every ecosystem.

`docker-compose.yml` defines eight services (backend, worker, frontend, postgres, redis, mailcrab, indicator-service, mcp-gateway) with every published port interpolated from the root `.env` (BACKEND_PORT 8001, BACKEND_DEBUG_PORT 8090, WORKER_DEBUG_PORT 8091, FRONTEND_PORT 8002, POSTGRES_PORT 5432, MAILCRAB_PORT 8003, INDICATOR_SERVICE_PORT 8004, MCP_GATEWAY_PORT 8005); both Go sidecars are built from their own directories and bound to host loopback only, the backend mounts the host Docker socket with a matching `group_add` Docker GID so testcontainers-backed tests can start a throwaway Postgres, and backend, worker and frontend run as uid/gid 1000:1000 with the uv cache and venv redirected under /app/.cache.

The tracked root `.env.example` is the single configuration source for the dev stack: `backend` and `worker` load it via `env_file`, Compose interpolates port/URL/`DOCKER_GID` variables from it, and the `frontend` service receives `VITE_*` plus `JWT_SECRET: "${SECRET_KEY:?SECRET_KEY must be set in the root .env}"`, so the SSR route guard verifies tokens with exactly the backend signing key and Compose fails fast when `SECRET_KEY` is missing.

For parallel work, `scripts/setup-agent-worktree.sh <worktree-path> <branch-name> [base-ref]` creates a git worktree — attaching the branch when it already exists, otherwise branching from `base-ref` (default `origin/main`) — and writes a worktree root `.env` seeded from the main checkout's `.env`, falling back to `.env.example` and failing when neither exists; it then deletes and re-appends `COMPOSE_PROJECT_NAME` (derived from the worktree directory name), `DOCKER_GID` and all eight discovered free ports (BACKEND_PORT, FRONTEND_PORT, BACKEND_DEBUG_PORT, WORKER_DEBUG_PORT, POSTGRES_PORT, MAILCRAB_PORT, INDICATOR_SERVICE_PORT, MCP_GATEWAY_PORT), so re-runs leave no stale entries and concurrent agents get independent Compose projects without file or Docker conflicts.

`./scripts/agent-test` is the primary test entrypoint for agents (shorthand `just test …`), running on the host through `docker compose exec -T <service>` unless already inside a container or `--local` is given, sanitizing output and hard-capping it at `--max-chars` (default 3000).

The harness has three gates: Gate 0 runs lint/type checks (backend `ruff check`, `ruff format --check`, `ty check`; frontend `svelte-kit sync`, `svelte-check`, `eslint -f json`, `prettier --check .`) and halts without running any tests on failure; Gate 1 runs a path target with fail-fast; Gate 2 auto-detects ecosystems from the git diff and renders an Index plus Traces for the first 1–2 failures.

`justfile` is the command surface around the agent harness: `just test` (→ `./scripts/agent-test`), `just test-backend`, `just test-frontend`, `just check` (Gate 0 plus `just lint-go`) and `just up` (which resolves DOCKER_GID via `scripts/docker-gid.sh`), plus the host-toolchain recipes `just lint-go`, `just test-indicator-service`, `just test-mcp-gateway`, `just test-scripts` and `just test-all`, which is marked `[parallel]` and sweeps backend, frontend, both Go modules and the Node script suite; the harness itself exposes `--backend`, `--frontend`, `--all`, `--gate0-only`, `--no-gate0`, `--local`, `--json` and `--max-chars`.

The agent harness knows only the `backend` and `frontend` ecosystems; both Go services (`services/indicator-service` and `services/mcp-gateway`) are verified outside it — each through its own CI job and through `just test-indicator-service` / `just test-mcp-gateway` — and because `services/` is neither a backend nor a frontend prefix, a diff touching only Go files detects no ecosystem and Gate 2 falls back to running the backend and frontend suites.

Editing a backend model mandates generating an Alembic migration, and all migration files must follow the `<hash>_<description>.py` naming; manual SQL migrations should be created with the autogenerate command and use `op.execute()` inside the generated revision.

`migrations/env.py` imports every domain `model` module so all tables register on `BaseModel.metadata`, and overrides `sqlalchemy.url` from `DATABASE_URL`, rewriting `postgresql+asyncpg://` to synchronous `postgresql://` because Alembic runs a sync engine.

`src/commands/seed.py` always seeds reference data (`AccountTypeModel` and `InstitutionModel`), and only in the `dev` environment additionally seeds the test user, sample securities, accounts, positions, portfolios and integration users before committing.

`src/commands/flush_market_data.py` provides a mutually exclusive `--security-id <uuid>` or `--all` admin command that counts rows in `PriceModel` and `IntradayPriceModel`, requires an interactive `[y/N]` confirmation before deleting them, and invalidates the corresponding indicator cache (`invalidate_security` or `flush_all`).

`src/worker.py` builds a `MemoryHuey` instance in the `test` environment and a `RedisHuey` otherwise; its `on_startup` handler registers the worker's own `svcs` registry with a `NullPool` session manager (to avoid "operation in progress" errors across `asyncio.run()` cycles) and imports `src.account.task`, `src.integration.task` and `src.market.task` so their tasks are registered, while `on_shutdown` closes that registry.
Because the worker's `svcs` registry only exists inside a running Huey consumer, every task body guards on `huey.svcs_registry` and resolves its services through `Container(huey.svcs_registry)`.

The Huey dashboard is mounted by the FastAPI app at `/worker/api` by `src/main.py` calling `init_worker_dashboard`, which creates the huey-dashboard task table, registers Huey signal handlers with `bind_signals=True` and starts a Redis pub/sub listener; the task API is guarded by `current_user` and a WebSocket is exposed at `/worker/api/updates`.

The dev `worker` service sets `HUEY_DASHBOARD_WORKER: 1` so the Huey consumer process emits the signal events the dashboard subscribes to, and runs the consumer under `watchfiles` with `--periodic` so edits restart it and the periodic scheduler is armed; the prod worker command is `huey_consumer src.worker.huey -w 2 --worker-type thread` with neither `watchfiles` nor `--periodic`.

CI (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`) runs on push to `main` and on pull request opened/synchronize/reopened with four independent jobs: `backend` (Python 3.14, `uv sync --dev`, `uv run ty check`, `uv run ruff check && uv run ruff format --check`, `uv run pytest`), `frontend` (Node 25, `npm install` in `frontend/`, `npm run check`, `npm run lint`, `npm run test:run`, then `node --test scripts/opencode-go-session-fetch.test.mjs`, with job-level `VITE_*` and `JWT_SECRET` env), and two identically shaped Go jobs — `indicator-service` and `mcp-gateway` — on Go 1.27.1 running `go mod download`, `go vet ./...`, a `gofmt -l` check, `staticcheck@v0.8.1`, `govulncheck@v1.8.0`, `go build ./...` and `go test ./...`.

The `backend` CI job declares no Redis or PostgreSQL service because Redis is replaced by the autouse fake and PostgreSQL comes from the testcontainers fixture, so the suite must never depend on a real external service.

`docker-compose.prod.yml` keeps the same service shape minus mailcrab — seven services — with built images, `restart: always`, explicit `container_name`s and fixed published ports (backend `8000:8000`, frontend `80:3000`); both Go services are internal-network only with no published host port, the file declares no `env_file`, the worker runs `huey_consumer src.worker.huey -w 2 --worker-type thread`, Compose fails fast when `MARKET_DATA_SERVICE_TOKEN` is unset, and `ENVIRONMENT` defaults to `prod` for the Go services.

The root `Dockerfile` builds the backend image in two stages using `uv sync --frozen` (dependencies layer first, project second), copies the venv into a `python:3.14-slim` runtime as a non-root `appuser`, and runs `uvicorn src.main:app --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8000 --workers 4 --timeout-graceful-shutdown 30` on port 8000.

The frontend production image is a two-stage `node:20-alpine` build (`npm ci` plus `npm run build` with `VITE_API_BASE_URL`/`VITE_INTERNAL_API_URL` build args) whose runtime stage runs `node build` on port 3000, and both Go service images share one shape — `golang:1.27-alpine` builds a static `CGO_ENABLED=0` binary with `-ldflags="-s -w"` from `./cmd/<service>` into `alpine:3.21`, installed with `ca-certificates`, `tzdata` and `wget` for the healthcheck, run as the non-root `appuser` and exposing 8080.

Migrations are not a deployment step: `lifespan_context` in `src/main.py` calls `run_migrations()` through `asyncio.to_thread` unless `settings.environment == 'test'`, and `run_migrations()` executes `alembic.command.upgrade(Config('alembic.ini'), 'head')`, so each backend instance upgrades the database to head as it starts.

Health probes are split by intent: `GET /health/live` returns `{'status': 'alive'}` without touching dependencies and is the check wired into the Compose healthchecks and Dockerfile `HEALTHCHECK`, while `GET /health/ready` runs `select(1)` through the container-resolved `AsyncSession` and pings Redis, returning 200 with per-dependency `ok` values or 503 with `{'status': 'degraded', …}`.

Both dev and prod Compose files healthcheck each Go sidecar by calling `wget -qO- http://localhost:8080/health` (the dev mcp-gateway check uses `$$PORT`), and the two services together expose `GET /health` plus `POST /compute` (indicator-service) and `GET /health` plus the MCP streamable HTTP endpoint at `/mcp` (mcp-gateway); both shut down gracefully on SIGINT/SIGTERM within a 10-second grace period.

This repository uses OpenSpec in `spec-driven` mode as declared by `openspec/config.yaml`; canonical specs live in `openspec/specs/<capability>/spec.md`, active changes in `openspec/changes/<name>/`, and archived changes in `openspec/changes/archive/YYYY-MM-DD-<name>/`.

The four OpenSpec stages — propose, explore, apply and archive — are each defined once per agent tool, so they exist in four mirrored tool directories: `.agent/` (`workflows/opsx-*.md` plus `skills/openspec-*/`), `.opencode/` (`command/opsx-*.md` plus `skills/openspec-*/`), `.github/` (`prompts/opsx-*.prompt.md` plus `skills/openspec-*/`) and `.claude/` (`commands/opsx/{propose,explore,apply,archive}.md` plus `skills/openspec-*/`); `CLAUDE.md` does not exist in this checkout, so Claude Code is served by the `.claude/` directory directly.

`/opsx:propose` creates a change with `openspec new change "<name>"`, then builds artifacts in dependency order using `openspec status --change <name> --json` and `openspec instructions <artifact-id> --change <name> --json`, reading completed dependency artifacts before writing each new one and never copying the agent-only `context` and `rules` blocks into the output files.

`/opsx:apply` reads the `contextFiles` returned by `openspec instructions apply`, implements each pending task with minimal focused changes, marks `- [ ]` → `- [x]` immediately, and pauses to ask for clarification (or suggests updating artifacts) when a task is unclear or reveals a design issue.

`/opsx:archive` never auto-selects a change (it lists them with `openspec list --json` and prompts when ambiguous), warns and requires confirmation for incomplete artifacts or unchecked tasks, compares delta specs at `openspec/changes/<name>/specs/` against `openspec/specs/<capability>/spec.md` before offering a sync, and moves the directory to `openspec/changes/archive/YYYY-MM-DD-<name>` (failing if that target already exists).
`/opsx:explore` is a thinking-only stance — reading, searching and creating OpenSpec artifacts are allowed, but implementing application code is not.

`.github/workflows/openwiki-update.yml` is scheduled daily at 08:00 UTC and can be dispatched manually; it installs `openwiki` globally with npm, first runs `node --test scripts/opencode-go-session-fetch.test.mjs`, then `openwiki code --update --print` with `OPENWIKI_PROVIDER=openai-compatible`, `OPENAI_COMPATIBLE_BASE_URL=https://opencode.ai/zen/go/v1`, `OPENWIKI_MODEL_ID=deepseek-v4.1-flash` and `OPENAI_COMPATIBLE_API_KEY` from the `OPENCODE_API_KEY` secret, plus a `NODE_OPTIONS` preload shim that for opencode.ai requests only injects the required `x-opencode-session` header and a non-generic user agent and round-trips `reasoning_content` back into outgoing assistant messages for thinking-mode models; it finally opens a PR on branch `openwiki/update` restricted to `add-paths: openwiki` with `docs: update OpenWiki` as message and title.

The OpenWiki block at the end of `AGENTS.md` (delimited by `<!-- OPENWIKI:START -->` / `<!-- OPENWIKI:END -->`) declares a retrieval-first consumption policy for the generated `openwiki/` tree, describing it as an optional just-in-time evidence index rather than required startup reading: agents must not enumerate, preload or search wikis at task start, they use `openwiki_search` for just-in-time context and `openwiki_read` for the relevant complete sections when the user asks or when unfamiliar architecture or dependency behavior materially affects the task, a `workspace_required` response means asking which listed workspace to use and retrying with its ID, `openwiki_list_workspaces`/`openwiki_list_wikis` exist for discovering workspace membership, and when the retrieval tools are unavailable the fallback is reading the `openwiki/quickstart.md` entry point and following its links.

`just up` resolves the host Docker socket's group id with `scripts/docker-gid.sh` before starting Compose: the script `stat`s the socket on Linux, asks the daemon through a throwaway `alpine:3` container on Darwin (where the socket is remounted with different ownership), and prints nothing when no socket is mounted, in which case Compose falls back to `DOCKER_GID:-959`.

`tests/test_migrations_autogenerate.py` guards model/migration drift: it drops the schema and `alembic_version`, upgrades to head, runs `alembic revision --autogenerate`, and fails if the generated revision contains any `op.` call, deleting the generated file afterwards.

The admin CLI commands are run inside the backend container, and `seed_data` is idempotent-by-lookup — it selects before inserting rather than relying on constraint violations — so repeated runs do not duplicate rows; `tests/commands/test_seed.py` pins this by running the seed twice and re-asserting the same row counts.

The agent harness writes machine-readable reports to `.cache/agent-test/backend.xml` for the backend and `frontend/.cache/agent-test/frontend.json` for the frontend (deleting any stale report first so a missing report is meaningful), and exits 1 when anything failed, errored, or the runner itself failed.

The skill catalogue is declared once in `.ai/skills/` (architecture-review, commit-message, feature-definition, orchestration, pr-review, quality-check, spec-writing, ticket-execution) and `.claude/skills/`, `.agent/skills/` and `.opencode/skills/` symlink each of them, while the four OpenSpec skills (`openspec-propose`, `openspec-explore`, `openspec-apply-change`, `openspec-archive-change`) stay per-tool copies — `.github/skills/` holds only those four — so adding an OpenSpec stage means adding every mirror (`.agent/workflows/`, `.opencode/command/`, `.claude/commands/opsx/`, `.github/prompts/`); `.opencode/opencode.json` sets `default_agent: "orchestrator"` with per-agent models (`arch-reviewer` on `opencode-go/grok-4.7`, `implementer` on `opencode-go/deepseek-v4.1-flash`, `orchestrator` and `pr-reviewer` on `opencode-go/glm-5.3-flash`, `spec-writer` on `opencode-go/deepseek-v4-pro`) and denies external-directory access to `/tmp/*` and `/private/tmp/*`.

The OpenWiki block in `AGENTS.md` keeps source code and tests authoritative (a brief's unknowns and review items are verification gaps rather than requirements), prefers the narrowest quiet validation that proves the changed behavior while preserving complete failure output, and instructs agents not to hand-edit generated OpenWiki pages but to update source code and docs and let the scheduled workflow regenerate the `openwiki/` tree.

`AGENTS.md` at the repository root is the entrypoint of the agent guidance hierarchy: it states the communication style (sparse, filler-free, ask when unsure instead of inferring), the branch and merge protection rule (agents never merge into `main`; ticket PRs merge into their `feat/<slug>` integration branch), the orchestration artifact table, delegation to `src/AGENTS.md`, `frontend/AGENTS.md` and `services/README.md`, the Docker-only-vs-host-Go command rule, the harness and worktree instructions, and ends with the OpenWiki block; the three area guides own their own command lists, the no-external-services testing rules, the DDD and rune-class layering contracts, and the Go `cmd`+`internal` conventions with no shared module.

The OpenSpec propose/apply/archive loop is a contract on a change directory: it is scaffolded by `openspec new change "<name>"` (never hand-written) and becomes apply-ready only when every artifact named in the schema's `apply.requires` has `status: "done"` — for `spec-driven` that is `proposal.md`, then `design.md` and delta specs, then `tasks.md` — and archive-ready when its tasks are checked and delta specs are reconciled against `openspec/specs/<capability>/spec.md` before the move to `openspec/changes/archive/YYYY-MM-DD-<name>`.

The agent tooling is layered one owner per concern: `.ai/skills/` is the authoritative shared skill catalogue, `.claude/agents/`, `.agent/agents/` and `.opencode/agents/` hold thin tool-specific agent definitions (Claude Code `tools:`/`model:` frontmatter, Antigravity `invoke_subagent` style with sandboxed command policy, opencode `mode:`/`permissions:` plus an extra `orchestrator`), the same four OpenSpec stages are mirrored in `.agent/workflows/`, `.opencode/command/`, `.claude/commands/opsx/` and `.github/prompts/`, and `.ai/` is the durable output area — `features/`, `reviews/` (`<date>-architecture[-<focus>].md`), `notes/` (`<id>-plan.md`) and the gitignored `scratch/`.

The orchestration skill defines a ticket pipeline over GitHub issues labeled `ticket` plus exactly one `status:*`, managed with the `gh` CLI, created directly as `status:planned` and transitioning planned → in-progress → in-review → approved or changes-requested, with `in-progress` → `pending` when a plan is fundamentally wrong, a maximum of three review cycles before escalation, and dependencies gated on every `depends_on` id being closed; the orchestrator owns every label transition and closure (workers never touch labels), squash-merges approved-and-green ticket PRs into the ticket's `feat/<slug>` integration branch without asking, and stops at the end with one `feat/<slug>` → `main` PR that the user reviews and merges.

The harness's Gate 2 auto-detection ignore list is `openspec/`, `openwiki/`, `.github/`, `.opencode/`, `.agent/`, `.claude/`, `.ai/`, `scripts/` and `frontend/node_modules/`, and `--gate0-only` combined with `--no-gate0` exits 0 immediately without running anything; when the rendered output exceeds `--max-chars`, at least half the budget is reserved for the Traces half so an oversized Index cannot starve the failure detail.

`openspec/config.yaml` contains only `schema: spec-driven` — the `context` and per-artifact `rules` blocks are commented-out examples, so this repository defines no extra project context or artifact rules for OpenSpec.

Two habits keep the change loop honest in practice: a backend model edit always ships its `docker compose exec backend uv run alembic revision --autogenerate -m "<msg>"` migration in the same change, and temporary artifacts (issue-body and PR payloads, captured output) go to `.ai/scratch/` — which is gitignored — with working notes in `.ai/notes/`, never the repository root or `/tmp`.

`frontend/AGENTS.md` defines a four-layer frontend contract: `.svelte` files hold markup, styling and simple view state; `.svelte.ts` files hold rune-based ES6 classes for state and business logic (never destructured primitives, never module-level instances, `$effect` only for side effects); stateless `.ts` API clients own HTTP concerns; and chart drawing tools live in per-plugin directories under `frontend/src/lib/components/charts/plugins/<plugin-name>/` with a fixed module layout, strict no-cross-plugin imports, shared plumbing in `plugins/helpers/` and pure financial math in `$lib/utils/finance/`.

The dev and prod Compose files select different build targets for the same services: dev runs `backend` and `worker` from the published `ghcr.io/astral-sh/uv:python3.14-bookworm` image (bind-mounting the repo and running `uv sync` at container start) and `frontend` from `node:latest`, building only `indicator-service` and `mcp-gateway` from `./services/<name>`; prod builds `backend` from the root `Dockerfile`, `frontend` from `./frontend`, and both Go services from their own directories, using the `postgres:18` and `redis:7-alpine` images directly.

Both Go CI jobs tolerate a `govulncheck` failure only when every finding is a Go standard-library CVE (known under the pinned Go 1.27.1 and fixed in a later patch release) and no finding comes from a module, so any module vulnerability still fails the job.

The orchestration artifact table pins where each work product lives and how its lifecycle is tracked: feature spec at `.ai/features/<slug>.md` (draft → ready → done, produced by the `feature-definition` skill), architecture review at `.ai/reviews/<YYYY-MM-DD>-architecture[-<focus>].md` (open → resolved, produced by `architecture-review`), ticket as a GitHub issue labeled `ticket` + `status:*` (produced by `spec-writing`), PR review verdict appended to the ticket's `## Review feedback` (produced by `pr-review`), optional working notes at `.ai/notes/<id>-plan.md`, and gitignored scratch payloads in `.ai/scratch/`.

Workers map one-to-one onto skills (`spec-writer`→`spec-writing`, `implementer`→`ticket-execution`, `pr-reviewer`→`pr-review`, `arch-reviewer`→`architecture-review`) and the orchestration skill documents the per-tool spawn binding: Claude Code uses the `Agent` tool by `subagent_type` and `SendMessage` to continue the same agent, opencode uses the `subagent` tool by worker name, Antigravity uses `invoke_subagent` by agent name, and parallel work is isolated through `scripts/setup-agent-worktree.sh` in every case — Antigravity's `branch` workspace still requires the script's `.env` port logic.
